title: Session snapshot retroactive credit correction for intermittent streaming clients
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Intermittent clients that disconnect and later resume over websocket/HTTP-stream are sometimes double-charged or left under-credited due to stale session snapshots and delayed finalization of token tallies. This manifests when (a) prefix chunks are cached locally (KV cache), (b) server-side finalization executes after a stale snapshot is applied, or (c) client and proxy replay fragments out of order. Goal: implement a deterministic retroactive-credit-correction mechanism that can detect finalized sessions whose snapshots diverge from canonical token tallies and issue compensating credits/debits without affecting idempotency guarantees. Scope: server-side metering pipeline and session checkpointing components only; we will not change client SDK protocols in this ticket.

Investigation notes: We reproduced with a fuzz harness that simulates reconnect + partial replay + delayed finalization. Root causes identified: (1) snapshot checkpointing writes a per-session 'finalized_offset' sometimes after token tally persists; race with async checkpoint compaction leads to undercount; (2) dedupe tokens across multiplexed fragments relied on best-effort frame ids from proxies which can be non-monotonic after failover.

Design proposal summary:
- Add a retroactive reconciliation pass that runs as an eventual consistency job for sessions marked 'closed-with-reconnect' within the last 72 hours. The job will compute canonical token tallies from transaction logs and compare to stored session tallies.
- When divergence > threshold (e.g., 1 token or >0.1%), create a compensating billing adjustment record and emit an audit event. Adjustments will be stored as idempotent objects keyed by session_id + reconciliation_run_id.
- Introduce a small on-path change: persist an additional monotonic sequence watermark at checkpoint commit time (checkpoint_seq) to reduce races. This is backward compatible; older checkpoints without watermark will be included in reconciliation but processed with caution.
- Implement stricter proto dedup heuristics for fragment IDs: prefer server-assigned monotonic ids if present; fall back to client-provided ids with collision detection.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'retroactive_metering_correction' default off.
2) Deploy reconciliation job (read-only) to run in dry-run mode and produce a reconciliation report for a week. Verify false positive rate < 0.5% and inspect customer impact surface using dashboards.
3) If metrics look good, enable compensating write path for a small subset of customers (internal shadow tenants) for two weeks.
4) Gradual enablement to full fleet with monitoring alerts and a manual kill-switch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reconciliation job can run for 10k closed-with-reconnect sessions in under 30 minutes in staging.
- No more than 0.1% of affected sessions produce >1 token discrepancy in dry-run.
- Compensating adjustments are idempotent and visible in billing reconciliation dashboard.
- No regression in normal streaming latency (p95 increase < 5ms) with feature on.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New Grafana panel: reconciliation-run results (sessions processed, matches, discrepancies by magnitude, top 10 customers impacted).
- Alert: daily discrepancy_count > 100 => page on-call metering eng.
- Emit structured audit events to S3 for legal/finance review.

Backwards compatibility and risk mitigation:
- Reconciliation is eventual and only issues compensating records after operator approval in early phases.
- If reconciliation detects a negative-correction (refund), finance workflow will require human review for high-value customers (> $1000/day).

Notes on quota/rate-limit interplay:
- Reconciliations that generate compensating credits must also adjust quota state so customers do not get double credits that inadvertently expand active quotas. The job will write an atomic pair: billing adjustment + quota_delta marker.
